learning.why: book-coin example showed directly that even if the object is same, one person can't see what's behind from their side

end.summary:
Practised top, front and side views of solids and objects.
Matched views to objects correctly in 6 of 6 attempts.
Described solid views correctly without help in 2 of 3 attempts.
Explained why views change from different places in 5 of 8 attempts.
The view misconception was corrected later; drawing only visible parts was not yet corrected after the last example.
end.parentNote: Reyansh practised describing and matching top, front and side views. They used the visible shape to identify a circle, rectangle, triangle and square, and corrected the idea that another person always sees the same view. They still sometimes included a hidden part, such as a cup handle, in a view; this was not corrected after the last related example. At home, place a cup or toy behind a book and ask Reyansh to draw only what can be seen from one position.
